name: ctl_ioctl
prose: Slice cut the head and tail: static int ctl_ioctl(struct cdev *dev, u_long cmd, caddr_t addr, int flag, struct thread *td) is at ctl.c:2583-3633. Precondition: dev->si_drv1 is the CTL softc and addr points to the argument structure for cmd, which the function both reads and writes. Postcondition: retval starts at 0 and the function has a switch on cmd. It returns retval at 3632, except that CTL_LUN_MAP returns ENXIO directly (without the lock held) when lm->port is outside [port_min, port_max) or has no port (3496-3501) and when a non-UNSET mapping names a LUN that does not exist (3520-3521). Cases: CTL_IO returns ctl_ioctl_io's result. CTL_ENABLE_PORT, CTL_DISABLE_PORT and CTL_SET_PORT_WWNS walk the port list under ctl_lock: a port is acted on if entry->port_type is CTL_PORT_NONE and targ_port matches (then the loop stops after that port), or if entry->port_type & port->port_type is nonzero; for CTL_SET_PORT_WWNS the second kind of match prints a message, sets retval = EINVAL and stops the loop without changing the port, so a port-type match always gives EINVAL for SET_PORT_WWNS (2615-2670); enable/disable drop ctl_lock around ctl_port_online/ctl_port_offline. CTL_GET_OOA returns EINVAL for alloc_len == 0, alloc_num == 0, alloc_len != alloc_num * sizeof(struct ctl_ooa_entry), or (without CTL_OOA_FLAG_ALL_LUNS) a lun_num out of range or absent (2681-2712); otherwise it allocates entries, fills them via ctl_ioctl_fill_ooa under ctl_lock, sets fill_num = min(found, alloc_num) and fill_len, copies the entries out (retval = the copyout result), then sets cur_bt and dropped_num/status (CTL_OOA_NEED_MORE_SPACE when found > alloc_num, else CTL_OOA_OK) even if the copyout failed, and frees entries (2700-2747). CTL_DELAY_IO sets only delay_info->status: NOT_IMPLEMENTED when CTL_IO_DELAY is not compiled in, else INVALID_LUN (return path leaves it) or OK/INVALID_TYPE then INVALID_LOC, and when the LUN exists and the location is valid the delay type/seconds are stored in the LUN even if the type was invalid (2755-2790); retval stays 0. CTL_ERROR_INJECT returns EINVAL for a bad LUN (2803-2811), otherwise appends a copy of the descriptor to the LUN's error_list, assigns the next error_serial to it and to the caller's copy, retval 0. CTL_ERROR_INJECT_DELETE returns EINVAL for a bad LUN or when no descriptor with the serial exists, otherwise frees all descriptors with that serial (2847-2874). CTL_DUMP_STRUCTS prints PR keys of enabled LUNs, ports and frontends and returns 0. CTL_LUN_REQ finds the backend by name; backend not found, args too long (> CTL_MAX_ARGS_LEN), copyin failure or an nvlist unpack failure set lun_req->status = CTL_LUN_ERROR and an error_str with retval left 0 (2949-2983); otherwise it calls backend->ioctl (retval is its result), destroys the args nvlist, and packs result_nvl out to lun_req->result, with CTL_LUN_ERROR set on pack, size or copyout failure (those error returns do not destroy result_nvl, 2996-3019). CTL_LUN_LIST builds an XML sbuf of fixed size alloc_len under ctl_lock; sbuf allocation failure, or running out of space, sets list->status (CTL_LUN_LIST_ERROR or CTL_LUN_LIST_NEED_MORE_SPACE) and leaves retval 0; on success it copies out and retval is the copyout result (3064-3206); in that loop a LUN whose backend is NULL is skipped with continue at 3106 before the mtx_unlock(&lun->lun_lock) at 3181. CTL_ISCSI and CTL_NVMF forward to the frontend's ioctl or set status to an error when the frontend is missing; CTL_PORT_REQ and CTL_PORT_LIST are analogous to LUN_REQ and LUN_LIST for ports (3242-3490); CTL_LUN_MAP sets up or removes LUN mappings and announces the port (3491-3531); CTL_GET_LUN_STATS and CTL_GET_PORT_STATS copy stats out until alloc_len would be exceeded (3532-3597). Any other cmd sets retval = ENOTTY (3628). Partly read: the bodies of CTL_PORT_REQ (3242-3334) and CTL_PORT_LIST (3335-3490) were only skimmed by their returns, not read line by line.
note: ctl.c:2583-3633, slice cut head; read 2583-3330 and 3491-3633 in full, partly read: CTL_PORT_REQ/CTL_PORT_LIST 3242-3490 (only return/retval lines). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: CTL_SET_PORT_WWNS gives EINVAL on any port_type match (2624-2641), not only multiple ports. Old prose also called CTL_LUN_REQ errors EINVAL-ish; they are reported in lun_req->status with retval 0.

name: ctl_decode_lun
prose: Precondition: encoded is any 64-bit REPORT LUNS style LUN field. Postcondition: it writes encoded big-endian into an 8-byte array lun[] (so lun[0] holds the top byte) and returns a decoded uint32_t, starting from 0xffffffff (ctl.c:3761-3804). Switch on lun[0] & 0xc0: address method 0x00 (peripheral) returns lun[1] when (lun[0] & 0x3f) == 0 and lun[2..7] are all zero; address method 0x40 (flat) returns ((lun[0] & 0x3f) << 8) + lun[1] when lun[2..7] are all zero; address method 0xc0 (extended) switches on lun[0] & 0x0f: for 0x02 it switches on lun[0] & 0x30: 0x00 returns lun[1] (the other bytes are not checked), 0x10 returns (lun[1] << 16) + (lun[2] << 8) + lun[3] (bytes 4-7 not checked), 0x20 returns (lun[2] << 24) + (lun[3] << 16) + (lun[4] << 8) + lun[5] only when lun[1], lun[6] and lun[7] are zero, and 0x30 and any 0x20 case failing the zero test leave 0xffffffff; for extended address method 0x0f it explicitly sets 0xffffffff and any other extended method leaves 0xffffffff. Method 0x80 (logical unit addressing, RPL_LUNDATA_ATYP_LUN) has no case and yields 0xffffffff. Any shape failing its checks yields 0xffffffff, which is also the value for a malformed input. The shift (lun[2] << 24) is done on an int, so it overflows for lun[2] >= 0x80 (signed overflow in C). No memory, lock or reference is taken.
note: ctl.c:3761-3804, macros scsi_all.h:3045-3053. The earlier prose is correct on structure but said 'returns 0xffffffff for every other encoding' - true only after the per-case checks above; the earlier contract (rejected by Frama-C) omitted the unchecked bytes in the 0x00/0x10 extended cases. Contract left empty because of the signed-shift UB at line 3791.

name: ctl_pro_preempt
prose: Slice cut the head: static int ctl_pro_preempt(softc, lun, res_key, sa_res_key, type, residx, ctsio, cdb, param) is at ctl.c:7910-8164. Precondition: the caller does not hold lun->lun_lock; ctsio is an in-flight PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT with parsed res_key, sa_res_key, type, residx. Postcondition: it takes lun_lock at once (7918) and every return path below releases it first. Branch A (sa_res_key == 0 and lun->pr_res_idx == CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS): returns 1 after ctl_set_invalid_field and ctl_done when the scope is not SPR_LU_SCOPE or the type is > 8, 2, 4 or 0, without freeing ctsio->kern_data_ptr (7922-7945); otherwise it clears every other registrant's key with a CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT unit attention, sets pr_key_count = 1, pr_res_type = type, sets pr_res_idx = residx unless the type is one of the all-registrants types, increments pr_generation, unlocks and sends a CTL_PR_PREEMPT HA message, then falls to return 0 (7951-7976, 8163). Branch B (sa_res_key == 0 and not all-registrants): frees kern_data_ptr, sets invalid field, ctl_done, returns 1 (7977-7988). Branch C (sa_res_key != 0 and either all-registrants or no reservation held, 7990): if res_key == sa_res_key it frees kern_data_ptr, sets invalid field, completes and returns 1 (7994-8014); else it clears every key equal to sa_res_key (pr_key_count-- and a unit attention each); if none was found it unlocks, frees kern_data_ptr, sets a reservation conflict, completes the I/O and returns CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE (0 as the return value, 8026-8031); if found it increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0. Branch D (sa_res_key != 0 and a reservation is held by a specific registrant): if sa_res_key equals that holder's key it checks scope and type as in branch A (invalid-field return 1 without freeing kern_data_ptr, 8052-8074), then clears the key of each registrant other than residx that equals sa_res_key, sends CTL_UA_RES_RELEASE to the rest when the reservation type changes from a registrants-only type, sets pr_res_type = type and pr_res_idx (to residx, or CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS for the all-registrants types), increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0 (8091-8123); if sa_res_key does not equal the holder's key it clears every matching key, and when none was found it unlocks, frees kern_data_ptr, sets a reservation conflict, completes and returns 1 (8141-8147), else increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0 (8148-8160). So the 'not found' paths return 0 in branch C and 1 in branch D, and the invalid scope/type returns do not free kern_data_ptr.
note: ctl.c:7910-8164 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (conflict path returns CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE at 8031 in branch C); round-15 reviewer mixed: RIGHT for branch C (8026-8031 returns 0), but branch D's not-found path returns 1 (8141-8147), so the old statement was true for one of the two not-found paths.

name: ctl_pro_preempt_other
prose: Slice cut the head: static void ctl_pro_preempt_other(struct ctl_lun *lun, union ctl_ha_msg *msg) is at ctl.c:8167-8231. Precondition: msg is a PERS_ACTION/CTL_PR_PREEMPT HA message from the peer with sa_res_key, res_type and residx; the function takes no lock and has no mtx_assert, so the caller is expected to hold the LUN lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It decodes sa_res_key and then: (1) if pr_res_idx is CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS or CTL_PR_NO_RESERVATION, or sa_res_key differs from the key of the current holder (ctl_get_prkey(lun, pr_res_idx)), then (1a) when sa_res_key == 0 it clears the key of every initiator other than msg residx that has a nonzero key and establishes CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT for it, sets pr_key_count = 1, sets pr_res_type from the message and sets pr_res_idx = msg residx unless the type is one of the all-registrants types (then pr_res_idx is left unchanged) (8182-8195); (1b) when sa_res_key != 0 it loops over all CTL_MAX_INITIATORS slots and, for each slot whose key is not equal to sa_res_key (including slots whose key is 0, i.e. unregistered ones), calls ctl_clr_prkey, decrements pr_key_count and establishes CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT; it changes neither pr_res_type nor pr_res_idx (8197-8204). (2) Otherwise (sa_res_key equals the holder's key) it loops over initiators other than msg residx with a nonzero key: a key equal to sa_res_key is cleared with pr_key_count-- and CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT, while other registrants get CTL_UA_RES_RELEASE when the message's type differs from the old pr_res_type and the old type is SPR_TYPE_WR_EX_RO or SPR_TYPE_EX_AC_RO; then pr_res_type is set from the message and pr_res_idx to the message's residx, or to CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS for the all-registrants types (8207-8227). In all three branches pr_generation is incremented once at the end (8229). It takes no lock, allocates nothing and sends no message.
note: ctl.c:8167-8231 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (the sa_res_key != 0 branch does not update type or index, 8197-8204; clears nonmatching keys there and matching keys in branch 2). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: that branch's loop does not skip key-0 slots, so it also decrements pr_key_count for unregistered slots (8198-8202).

name: ctl_backend_ramdisk_scsi_config_write
prose: Precondition: io is a SCSI I/O for a ramdisk LUN; the function contains no CTL_IO_ASSERT and does not validate the opcode beforehand (ctl_backend_ramdisk.c:819-872). Postcondition: it switches on io->scsiio.cdb[0] and returns retval, which is 0 except in the default case. SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE and SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE_16 set success and call ctl_config_write_done. START_STOP_UNIT: if any power-condition bits (SSS_PC_MASK) are set it sets success and completes without touching the LUN; otherwise with SSS_START it calls ctl_lun_has_media when SSS_LOEJ is also set and then ctl_start_lun, and without SSS_START it calls ctl_stop_lun and, with SSS_LOEJ, ctl_lun_ejected; it then sets success and calls ctl_config_write_done. PREVENT_ALLOW sets success and calls ctl_config_write_done (853-856). WRITE_SAME_10 and WRITE_SAME_16 call ctl_backend_ramdisk_ws(io) and UNMAP calls ctl_backend_ramdisk_unmap(io); completion of the I/O in those two cases is left to those helpers (I did not check their completion paths here). Any other opcode sets invalid-opcode sense, calls ctl_config_write_done and sets retval = CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE, whose value is 0 (ctl_private.h:44), so the function returns 0 in every case.
note: ctl_backend_ramdisk.c:819-872; CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE is defined 0 in ctl_private.h:44, so the old 'returns CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE only for default' distinction is moot: all return values are 0. Orig reviewer RIGHT (PREVENT_ALLOW, 853-856); round-15 reviewer RIGHT: no CTL_IO_ASSERT in this function and invalid opcodes are handled (864-868). Helpers ws/unmap not read.

name: sddadump
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is static int sddadump(void *arg, void *virtual, off_t offset, size_t length) at mmc_da.c:2000-2065 (the packet name mmcsd_dump does not exist). Precondition: arg is a struct disk whose d_drv1 is an sdda_part with a valid softc; virtual points to at least (length / MMC_SECTOR_SIZE) * MMC_SECTOR_SIZE readable bytes; called in dump context. Postcondition: it returns ENXIO if softc->state != SDDA_STATE_NORMAL (2018-2019); returns 0 without any I/O if length / MMC_SECTOR_SIZE (a uint16_t count) is 0 (2021-2023), so a length under one sector is not an error here; returns EIO if the softc's currently selected partition is not this part (2025-2026). Otherwise it builds an XPT_MMC_IO CCB with CAM_DIR_OUT, retry_count 0 and a 15000 ms timeout, uses MMC_WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK when count > 1 else MMC_WRITE_BLOCK, sets the command argument to offset / MMC_SECTOR_SIZE and shifts it left by 9 (making a byte address) unless the card has CARD_FEATURE_SDHC (2040-2043), points the zeroed softc->mmcdata at virtual with length MMC_SECTOR_SIZE * count and MMC_DATA_WRITE, adds MMC_DATA_MULTI and a CMD12 stop command when count > 1 (2053-2058), and calls cam_periph_runccb with cam_periph_error and SF_NO_RECOVERY | SF_NO_RETRY (2060-2061). If that returns nonzero it prints 'Aborting dump due to I/O error.' (2062-2063). It returns that error, or 0 on success. The offset is not checked for sector alignment (integer division discards a remainder), and a trailing partial sector of length is not written. The caller keeps ownership of the buffer; no memory is allocated and no lock is taken in this function.
note: mmc_da.c:2000-2065, slice cut head, name outside slice was the only reviewer reason (4 rounds). The earlier prose is wrong: it claimed EINVAL for len < sector or unaligned offset; code returns 0 for count == 0 (2022-2023) and does not check alignment, and it missed ENXIO/EIO returns (2018-2026) and the <<9 for non-SDHC (2042-2043).

name: ndadone
prose: Precondition: periph is an nda periph with an nda_softc, done_ccb a completed NVMe CCB whose ccb_state & NDA_CCB_TYPE_MASK selects the case; for BUFFER_IO and TRIM the caller does not hold the periph lock. Postcondition (nvme_da.c:1186-1300; returns nothing): BUFFER_IO and TRIM take the periph lock (1205). If the status is not CAM_REQ_CMP it calls ndaerror(done_ccb, 0, 0): on ERESTART it unlocks and returns, leaving the CCB outstanding for the retry, with no bio completed, no CCB release and outstanding_cmds not decremented (1207-1211); otherwise it releases the devq freeze if CAM_DEV_QFRZN is set. If the status is CAM_REQ_CMP and CAM_DEV_QFRZN is set it panics with 'REQ_CMP with QFRZN' (1220-1221), otherwise error = 0. For BUFFER_IO it sets bp->bio_error = error, bio_resid = bio_bcount and BIO_ERROR on error else bio_resid = 0, decrements outstanding_cmds, calls cam_iosched_bio_complete, releases the CCB, calls ndaschedule, unlocks and calls biodone(bp) (1224-1247). For TRIM it moves the request's bio list to a local queue, frees the trim request, completes the first bio via cam_iosched_bio_complete, releases the CCB, decrements outstanding_cmds, calls ndaschedule and unlocks, then for each queued bio sets bio_error, on error sets BIO_ERROR and bio_resid = bp1->bio_bcount (the first bio's count, not its own, 1280), else bio_resid = 0, calls cam_iosched_bio_complete for all but the first bio and biodone on each (1248-1286); then returns. NDA_CCB_DUMP and NDA_CCB_PASS return without releasing the CCB (1290-1295); any other state falls out of the switch to xpt_release_ccb(done_ccb) (1299).
note: nvme_da.c:1186-1300 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (ERESTART returns without completing the bio, decrementing, or releasing the CCB, 1208-1211). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: success with CAM_DEV_QFRZN panics (1220-1221); devq release happens only on the error path (1213-1214). Additional: trim error path sets resid from bp1 (1280).

name: nvme_probe_done
prose: Precondition: done_ccb is the completed CCB of the probe started by nvme_probe_start for periph, softc->action is NVME_PROBE_IDENTIFY_CD or NVME_PROBE_IDENTIFY_NS when the CCB succeeded and softc->restart is clear (nvme_xpt.c:305-493). Postcondition (returns nothing): (1) If status != CAM_REQ_CMP it calls cam_periph_error (adding SF_NO_RECOVERY | SF_NO_RETRY when softc->restart is set); on ERESTART it jumps to out: cam_release_devq(path, 0, 0, 0, FALSE) and returns, with nothing else changed (322-329). Otherwise it releases a frozen devq (xpt_release_devq) if CAM_DEV_QFRZN is set and falls to device_fail: it announces AC_LOST_DEVICE when the device is not CAM_DEV_UNCONFIGURED, sets the action to NVME_PROBE_INVALID, sets found = 0 and goes to done (346-350); this happens even when softc->restart is set. (2) If the CCB succeeded and softc->restart is set it goes to done directly without examining the data (352-353). (3) Otherwise it switches on softc->action: IDENTIFY_CD byte-swaps the controller data, copies it into path->device->nvme_cdata (allocating it with M_NOWAIT; allocation failure prints and goes to device_fail), replaces serial_num with a newly allocated string when that allocation succeeds, calls nvme_device_transport, sets the action to NVME_PROBE_IDENTIFY_NS, releases the CCB, calls xpt_schedule and jumps to out (355-393); IDENTIFY_NS byte-swaps the namespace data, goes to device_fail if nsze == 0, copies the data into nvme_data (allocating with M_NOWAIT, failure goes to device_fail), rebuilds device_id from nguid and eui64 when either is nonzero (leaving it NULL if that allocation fails), then for a CAM_DEV_UNCONFIGURED device clears the flag, acquires the device and announces AC_FOUND_DEVICE, else announces AC_GETDEV_CHANGED, and sets the action to NVME_PROBE_DONE and falls to done (394-470); any other action panics, including NVME_PROBE_DONE, which has no case (471-472). (4) At done: if softc->restart is set it clears it, releases the CCB, calls nvme_probe_schedule and goes to out (drop the devq freeze and return; the periph is not invalidated and queued request CCBs are not completed); otherwise it releases the CCB, completes every CCB on softc->request_ccbs with CAM_REQ_CMP, or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR when found is 0, drops the devq freeze, calls cam_periph_invalidate and cam_periph_release_locked (475-492).
note: nvme_xpt.c:305-493 read in full. Orig reviewer mixed: RIGHT for ERESTART (326-329) and for the success-with-restart path (352-353, 475-479) which skip marking lost and completing queued CCBs, but WRONG for a failed CCB with restart set, which reaches device_fail (346-350) first and marks the device lost. Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the switch (354-473) has no NVME_PROBE_DONE case and panics.

name: cdstart
prose: Precondition: the periph lock is held (cam_periph_assert MA_OWNED, scsi_cd.c:883), start_ccb is a CCB for this periph. Postcondition (cdstart at 877-1118; returns nothing): it switches on softc->state; there is no default case, so a state with no case leaves start_ccb unreleased. CD_STATE_NORMAL (889-967): bp = first bio in bio_queue. If bp is NULL: when softc->tur is set it clears tur and dispatches a TEST UNIT READY (ccb_state CD_CCB_TUR) with xpt_action, otherwise it releases start_ccb. If bp is not NULL: when softc->tur is set it clears tur and calls cam_periph_release_locked(periph) (908-911); it removes bp from the queue; if bp is not BIO_READ or BIO_WRITE it calls biofinish(bp, NULL, EOPNOTSUPP), releases start_ccb and returns at once without the reschedule step (914-918), even if more bios are queued; otherwise it builds a read/write CCB (READ_CD with a 12-byte CDB when blksize == 2352), sets ccb_state to CD_CCB_BUFFER_IO (OR CD_CCB_RETRY_UA and clearing CD_FLAG_RETRY_UA when set), inserts it in pending_ccbs, increments outstanding_cmds, sets ccb_bp = bp, re-reads bp as the next queued bio, and calls xpt_action (921-960). After the NORMAL branch, xpt_schedule(periph, CAM_PRIORITY_NORMAL) is called if bp (the next bio, or NULL) is non-NULL or softc->tur is set; since tur was cleared on every path that reaches this test, in practice only a remaining bio triggers the reschedule (962-965). CD_STATE_PROBE and CD_STATE_MEDIA_SIZE: malloc of read-capacity data with M_NOWAIT; on failure it prints, releases start_ccb and calls cam_periph_invalidate only when state is PROBE (975-992); otherwise it sets default d_sectorsize = 2048 and d_mediasize = 0 on the disk and dispatches a READ CAPACITY with ccb_state CD_CCB_PROBE or CD_CCB_MEDIA_SIZE (1000-1016). CD_STATE_MEDIA_ALLOW and CD_STATE_MEDIA_PREVENT: for PREVENT with CD_FLAG_DISC_LOCKED set it sets state CD_STATE_MEDIA_SIZE, releases start_ccb and calls xpt_schedule (1026-1031); otherwise it dispatches a PREVENT/ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL with ccb_state CD_CCB_MEDIA_ALLOW or CD_CCB_MEDIA_PREVENT. CD_STATE_MEDIA_TOC_HDR, TOC_FULL and TOC_LEAD: zero softc->toc (or softc->leadout), build a READ TOC CCB with the matching CD_CCB_MEDIA_TOC_* state and ccb_bp NULL, and call xpt_action (1051-1115). It does not release the periph other than in the tur case above.
note: scsi_cd.c:877-1118 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (EOPNOTSUPP return at 916-918 skips the reschedule). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: tur is cleared at 909 before the check at 962 (and also at 894 in the empty-queue branch); cam_periph_release_locked at 910 was omitted in the old text.

name: dastart
prose: Slice cut the head: static void dastart(struct cam_periph *periph, union ccb *start_ccb) is at scsi_da.c:3369-4086. Precondition: the periph lock is held (cam_periph_assert MA_OWNED, 3373); start_ccb was allocated for this periph. Postcondition (returns nothing): it switches on softc->state (label skipstate; no default case). DA_STATE_NORMAL: takes the next bio from cam_iosched_next_bio. If there is none, when DA_WORK_TUR is pending it sets DA_FLAG_TUR_PENDING, clears the flag and dispatches TEST UNIT READY (DA_CCB_TUR) with xpt_action, else it releases start_ccb (3387-3404). For a BIO_DELETE it calls softc->delete_func(periph, start_ccb, bp) and goes to out, or, with no delete_func, calls biofinish(bp, NULL, 0) and loops to take the next bio (3407-3418). Otherwise it clears a pending DA_WORK_TUR with da_periph_release_locked(periph, DA_REF_TUR), chooses an ordered or simple tag, and builds: for BIO_READ/BIO_WRITE a read/write CCB (a write sets DA_FLAG_DIRTY); for BIO_FLUSH, when the quirk DA_Q_NO_SYNC_CACHE is set or DA_FLAG_DIRTY is clear, biodone(bp) and goto skipstate (re-evaluating the state with the same start_ccb), else a SYNCHRONIZE CACHE and clears DA_FLAG_DIRTY; for BIO_ZONE it calls da_zone_cmd and if that returns an error or sets queue_ccb to 0 it finishes the bio with that error (dropping the periph lock around biofinish for ENOMEM), releases start_ccb and returns; any other bio command is finished with EOPNOTSUPP, start_ccb released, and the function returns (3437-3541). Otherwise it sets ccb_state DA_CCB_BUFFER_IO and CAM_UNLOCKED and the soft timeout, then at out inserts start_ccb in pending_ccbs (tagging DA_CCB_RETRY_UA and clearing DA_FLAG_RETRY_UA if set), sets ccb_bp = bp, increments softc->refcount, drops the periph lock around xpt_action and takes it again, then calls daschedule (3546-3563). The probe states: PROBE_WP skips to PROBE_RC16 or PROBE_RC (goto skipstate) when write-protect detection is off or mode_page < 0 or the 192-byte mode buffer malloc fails, else sends MODE SENSE; PROBE_RC, PROBE_RC16, PROBE_LBP, PROBE_BLK_LIMITS, PROBE_BDC and PROBE_CACHE allocate a result buffer with M_NOWAIT and, if the allocation fails, print and break without releasing or submitting start_ccb (3612-3616 is marked 'da_free_periph???'); PROBE_LBP, PROBE_BLK_LIMITS, PROBE_BDC skip to the next probe state when the VPD page is not supported; PROBE_ATA, if the ATA-information VPD page is unsupported, moves to PROBE_ZONE (goto skipstate) for host-aware or host-managed zone modes or calls daprobedone, else sends ATA IDENTIFY into periph->path->device->ident_data (not a malloc'd buffer, 3825); PROBE_ATA_LOGDIR, PROBE_ATA_IDDIR, PROBE_ATA_SUP and PROBE_ATA_ZONE call daprobedone (which finishes the probe with start_ccb) when their capability flag is clear, when the buffer malloc fails or when scsi_ata_read_log returns nonzero (freeing the buffer in the last case); otherwise they dispatch the read-log command; PROBE_ZONE calls daprobedone when the BDC VPD page is unsupported, releases start_ccb and prints when its malloc fails, else sends the VPD inquiry (4046-4083).
note: scsi_da.c:3369-4086, slice cut head; read in full except the argument lines of the scsi_* builder calls and the comment text. name: dadone
prose: Precondition: periph is a da periph, done_ccb a completed CCB from dastart (ccb_state type in DA_CCB_TYPE_MASK, ccb_bp the bio or NULL); the caller does not hold the periph lock (it is taken at 4658); softc->refcount >= 1 (KASSERT at 4775). Postcondition (scsi_da.c:4640-4813; returns nothing): if status != CAM_REQ_CMP it calls daerror(done_ccb, CAM_RETRY_SELTO, sf) with sf = SF_RETRY_UA when DA_CCB_RETRY_UA is set; on ERESTART it unlocks and returns without releasing the CCB, decrementing refcount or completing bp (4669-4673). On another nonzero error it either calls cam_periph_invalidate (error == ENXIO and DA_FLAG_PACK_INVALID not set) or flushes the iosched queues with ENXIO or EIO (4682-4721), and if bp != NULL sets bio_error = error, bio_resid = bio_bcount and BIO_ERROR; with error == 0 (daerror returned 0) and bp != NULL it sets bio_resid (0 for DA_CCB_DELETE, else csio->resid), bio_error = 0 and BIO_ERROR if resid != 0; then it releases a frozen devq (4727-4741). If status == CAM_REQ_CMP and bp != NULL: a CAM_DEV_QFRZN flag panics (4743-4744); BIO_ZONE calls dazonedone, else bio_resid is 0 for DELETE or csio->resid, BIO_ERROR is set when csio->resid > 0 for non-zone bios; bio_error is not assigned here except for the softc->error_inject case, which sets bio_error, resid = bio_bcount, BIO_ERROR and clears error_inject (4745-4758); with bp == NULL nothing is set. For all paths past the ERESTART return it removes the CCB from pending_ccbs, sets DA_FLAG_WAS_OTAG if the list became empty, calls cam_iosched_bio_complete, xpt_release_ccb and decrements refcount (4763-4776). For DA_CCB_DELETE it moves the delete_run_queue bios to a local queue, calls cam_iosched_trim_done and daschedule, unlocks and completes every queued bio with bio_error copied from bp (dereferencing bp, which is assumed non-NULL for deletes) and BIO_ERROR/resid from bp's flags (4777-4805); otherwise it calls daschedule and unlocks. Finally, if bp != NULL it calls biodone(bp) (4810-4811).

name: dadone_proberc
prose: Precondition: the periph lock is held (cam_periph_assert MA_OWNED, 4933); softc->state is DA_STATE_PROBE_RC or PROBE_RC16 and the CCB state is DA_CCB_PROBE_RC or DA_CCB_PROBE_RC16 (both only KASSERT-checked, 4914-4919); csio->data_ptr is the read-capacity buffer. Postcondition (scsi_da.c:4896-5167; returns nothing): it clears the announce buffer. On CAM_REQ_CMP: for READ CAPACITY(10) it takes block_size and maxsector from the data; if maxsector == 0xffffffff it frees rdcap, sets state DA_STATE_PROBE_RC16, releases the CCB, calls xpt_schedule and returns (4954-4960); for RC16 it takes length, address and lalba. A block_size of 0 is replaced by 512 (and maxsector 0 by -1) (4972-4976). If block_size >= maxphys it prints a message, sets announce_buf = NULL and calls cam_periph_invalidate; otherwise it calls dasetgeom, sets DA_FLAG_LBP when the lalba LBPME bit is set and DA_Q_NO_UNMAP is clear, and formats the announce string (4977-5006). On a non-CMP status it calls daerror(done_ccb, CAM_RETRY_SELTO, SF_RETRY_UA|SF_NO_PRINT): on ERESTART it returns at once without freeing csio->data_ptr, releasing the CCB or rescheduling (5016-5021); on another nonzero error it releases a frozen devq, then if the CCB is the RC16 one, DA_FLAG_CAN_RC16 is set and the status is CAM_REQ_INVALID or the sense is a current-error ILLEGAL REQUEST, it clears DA_FLAG_CAN_RC16, calls free(rdcap) (rdcap is NULL in the RC16 state, so csio->data_ptr is not freed), sets DA_STATE_PROBE_RC, releases the CCB, reschedules and returns (5050-5064); any other nonzero error either (when sense exists with ASC not 0x25 or 0x44, and not (asc 0x04 with ascq 0x02), and a current error) sets a 512-byte geometry with dasetgeom(periph, 512, -1, NULL, 0) and an 'Attempt to query device size failed' announce string, or prints the failure, sets announce_buf = NULL and calls cam_periph_invalidate (5093-5127). A daerror result of 0 on a failed status skips both branches. Every path that has not returned early then frees csio->data_ptr (5130), if announce_buf is non-NULL and DA_FLAG_ANNOUNCED is clear it prints the announcement and, if da_periph_acquire(DA_REF_SYSCTL) succeeds, queues the sysctl task (else prints an error) (5131-5156); finally if DA_FLAG_PROBED is set it calls daprobedone(periph, done_ccb) and returns, else it sets DA_STATE_PROBE_CACHE, releases the CCB, calls xpt_schedule and returns (5159-5167).

name: enc_runcmd
prose: Precondition: enc is an enclosure softc with a periph; cdb points to a command block (for SEMB types at least cdb[0] and cdb[2] are read without looking at cdbl; for other types cdbl bytes, clamped to IOCDBLEN, are copied); if dptr is non-NULL, dlenp points to an int whose sign selects direction. Postcondition (scsi_enc.c:575-645): dlen = *dlenp made positive, ddf = CAM_DIR_OUT when *dlenp was negative else CAM_DIR_IN, when dptr is non-NULL; dlen = 0 and CAM_DIR_NONE when dptr is NULL (583-593); cdbl > IOCDBLEN is clamped to IOCDBLEN (595-597). It gets a CCB with cam_periph_getccb(enc->periph, CAM_PRIORITY_NORMAL). For ENC_SEMB_SES and ENC_SEMB_SAFT it uses tdlen = ((min(dlen, 1020) + 3) & ~3) and fills an ATA I/O CCB (30 s timeout, data dptr/tdlen) with ATA_SEP_ATTN and the register values chosen by cdb[0]: RECEIVE_DIAGNOSTIC uses cdb[2] and 0x02, SEND_DIAGNOSTIC uses dptr[0] (0 if dlen == 0, reading dptr even when it is NULL) and 0x82, READ_BUFFER uses cdb[2] and 0x00, anything else uses dptr[0] (or 0 when dlen <= 0) and 0x80, each with count tdlen / 4 (600-618). Otherwise tdlen = dlen and a SCSI I/O CCB (60 s timeout, sense size sizeof(struct scsi_sense_data), cdb copied with bcopy of cdbl bytes) is filled (619-624). It runs cam_periph_runccb(ccb, enc_error, ENC_CFLAGS, ENC_FLAGS, NULL). If that returns nonzero and dptr is non-NULL it stores dlen (the positive requested length) in *dlenp (628-631); if it returns 0 and dptr is non-NULL it stores the CCB's residual (ataio.resid for XPT_ATA_IO, else csio.resid) plus (tdlen - dlen) in *dlenp (633-639); if dptr is NULL, *dlenp is not assigned. It then calls xpt_release_ccb(ccb) on all paths and returns the error from cam_periph_runccb (0 on success, 641-644).

name: sagetparams
prose: Slice cut the head: int sagetparams(periph, params_to_get, blocksize, density, numblocks, buff_mode, write_protect, speed, comp_supported, comp_enabled, comp_algorithm, tcs, prot_page, dp_size, prot_changeable) is at scsi_sa.c:3876-4200. Precondition: the output pointer for each SA_PARAM_* bit set in params_to_get is non-NULL (tcs and prot_page may be NULL); the caller may sleep. Postcondition: it gets a CCB (cam_periph_getccb) and chooses cpage = the device configuration page if SA_QUIRK_NO_CPAGE is set, else the data compression page (3894-3898). At retry it sizes a mode buffer and, if compression is requested, drops SA_PARAM_COMPRESSION from params_to_get when SA_QUIRK_NOCOMP is already set, otherwise adds sizeof(sa_comp_t) (3901-3909); it mallocs the buffer with M_NOWAIT and on NULL releases the CCB and returns ENOMEM (3912-3916). It runs MODE SENSE; if cam_periph_runccb returns EINVAL while compression was requested, then when cpage was the data compression page it switches to the device configuration page and goes to retry without freeing the current mode buffer (3939-3942, a leak of that buffer), else it sets SA_QUIRK_NOCOMP, frees the buffer and goes to retry (so that the retry runs without compression and does not write *comp_supported, *comp_enabled or *comp_algorithm); if the status is CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR it prints sense and goes to sagetparamsexit (3931-3950); other errors do not stop the decoding that follows. If blk_desc_len == 0 and both compression and other parameters were requested it shifts the data and issues a second MODE SENSE, going to the exit on error (3960-3992). It then stores each requested value: blocksize, numblocks, buff_mode, density, write_protect, speed through their pointers, and for compression comp_supported, comp_enabled, comp_algorithm (from the data compression page, or, for the device configuration page, comp_supported = TRUE and enabled from sel_comp_alg) and copies the compression page to tcs when non-NULL (3995-4036). With SA_PARAM_DENSITY_EXT and softc->scsi_rev >= SCSI_REV_SPC it issues REPORT DENSITY SUPPORT per density type; an error or non-CMP status is turned into error = 0 and density_info_valid[i] = 0 (breaking out when density_type_bits[i] == 0), otherwise density_info_valid[i] is the returned length (4038-4080). With SA_PARAM_LBP and SA_FLAG_PROTECT_SUPP it allocates a MODE SENSE(10) buffer (ENOMEM to the exit if that fails), runs it, and for a runccb error (error kept), a non-CMP status (EINVAL), a too-short reply (EINVAL), frees the buffer and exits; otherwise it fills softc->prot_info.cur_prot_state (method, pi_length, lbp_w/lbp_r/rbdp, initialized = 1), copies the subpage to prot_page when non-NULL and frees the buffer (4085-4183). At sagetparamsexit it releases the CCB and frees mode_buffer and returns error (4195-4199), which is 0 on success.

name: sasetparams
prose: Slice is a fragment of int sasetparams(periph, params_to_set, blocksize, density, calg, sense_flags) at scsi_sa.c:4391-4703. Precondition: periph is an sa periph; the caller may sleep (cam_periph_getccb, M_NOWAIT mallocs aside). Postcondition: it mallocs a sa_comp_t copy ccomp (M_NOWAIT) and returns ENOMEM if that fails (4412-4414); it calls sagetparams for the current blocksize, density, speed, buffer mode and compression page and, if that returns an error, frees ccomp and returns that error (4422-4431); it mallocs the mode buffer and on failure frees ccomp and returns ENOMEM (4437-4441); then gets a CCB. At retry it builds a MODE SELECT(6) header and block descriptor (blocksize and density from the arguments when requested, else the current values, SCSI_SAME_DENSITY for newer SCSI revisions, else media_density), copies ccomp into the compression page and, when compression is requested, edits it by page type (device configuration: set sel_comp_alg from calg or the saved algorithm; data compression: if the DCC bit is set set DCE/DCC and DDE and the algorithms; other page types fall to the unsupported case) (4450-4573). In the unsupported case it clears SA_PARAM_COMPRESSION, prints a message and, if nothing else was to be set, frees mode_buffer, releases the CCB and returns ENODEV without freeing ccomp (a leak, 4598-4601); otherwise it shortens the buffer and continues. It runs MODE SELECT with cam_periph_runccb; if that returns an error: when a block descriptor is present and neither density nor blocksize was being set it drops the descriptor and goes back to retry (the result of that retry replaces error); otherwise it rebuilds the buffer with the current blocksize and density and the original compression page, sets retry_count = 1 and runs a second MODE SELECT whose result is ignored (4632-4677). It then releases the CCB, frees ccomp (4679-4682), and when compression was requested clears SA_FLAG_COMP_ENABLED and saves comp_algorithm to saved_comp_algorithm and zeroes comp_algorithm when error is nonzero, else sets SA_FLAG_COMP_ENABLED and comp_algorithm = calg (4684-4698). Finally it frees mode_buffer and returns error, the result of the first MODE SELECT (or of the descriptor-less retry) (4701-4702); the second attempt's result is not part of it.

name: probedone
prose: Slice cut the head: static void probedone(struct cam_periph *periph, union ccb *done_ccb) is at scsi_xpt.c:1159-1814. Precondition: the periph lock is held (cam_periph_assert MA_OWNED, 1171); softc is a probe_softc whose request_ccbs queue is non-empty on any path that reaches the tail. Postcondition (returns nothing): it switches on softc->action. Three exit routes exist. (a) outr (1179-1182): after cam_periph_error returned ERESTART it calls cam_release_devq(path, 0, 0, 0, FALSE) and returns, leaving done_ccb queued for the retry (not released). (b) out (1193-1197): after the action's handler released done_ccb and called xpt_schedule it calls cam_release_devq and cam_periph_release_locked(periph) and returns. (c) the tail (1799-1814), reached by break: it dequeues the first CCB on softc->request_ccbs, sets its status to CAM_REQ_CMP and calls xpt_done; if the request queue is then empty it calls cam_release_devq, cam_periph_release_locked, cam_periph_invalidate and cam_periph_release_locked again, else it calls probeschedule and goes to out. Per action: PROBE_TUR ignores a non-ERESTART failure (releasing a frozen devq) and moves to PROBE_INQUIRY, releases the CCB and reschedules (route b). PROBE_INQUIRY/PROBE_FULL_INQUIRY: on CAM_REQ_CMP it marks CAM_DEV_INQUIRY_DATA_VALID and finds quirks; for a connected or offline logical unit it moves to PROBE_FULL_INQUIRY if the additional length exceeds SHORT_INQUIRY_LENGTH, else devises the transport and moves to PROBE_REPORT_LUNS (lun 0, ANSI revision above SPC2 and no NORPTLUNS quirk, rpl_size = 16), PROBE_MODE_SENSE (tagged queueing enabled) or PROBE_SUPPORTED_VPD_LIST, clears CAM_DEV_UNCONFIGURED and acquires the device if needed, releases the CCB, reschedules (route b); for a not-connected qualifier on lun 0 with ANSI revision >= SPC2 it also goes to PROBE_REPORT_LUNS; on failure (non-ERESTART) it clears CAM_DEV_INQUIRY_DATA_VALID; if control reaches 1291 (failure or an unsupported qualifier) it announces AC_LOST_DEVICE when the device is not CAM_DEV_UNCONFIGURED, sets PROBE_INVALID, releases the CCB and breaks (route c). PROBE_REPORT_LUNS: on failure it frees the data; if the list is longer than the buffer (nlun > maxlun) it frees the data, sets target->rpl_size = (nlun << 3) + 8, releases the CCB and reschedules with the action still PROBE_REPORT_LUNS (route b, 1324-1335); with nlun == 0 it frees the data; otherwise it swaps lun 0 to the front and calls probe_purge_old; then if the inquiry data is valid and connected/offline it moves to PROBE_MODE_SENSE or PROBE_SUPPORTED_VPD_LIST and reschedules (route b), else sets PROBE_INVALID, releases the CCB and breaks (route c). PROBE_MODE_SENSE, PROBE_SUPPORTED_VPD_LIST, PROBE_DEVICE_ID, PROBE_EXTENDED_INQUIRY, PROBE_SERIAL_NUM store or free the returned page, advance to the next action (MODE_SENSE then VPD list then DEVICE_ID then EXTENDED_INQUIRY then SERIAL_NUM; a failed VPD-list read jumps to the serial-number step) and use route b, except that SERIAL_NUM computes an MD5 checksum comparison when PROBE_INQUIRY_CKSUM is set (announcing AC_LOST_DEVICE if it changed and PROBE_NO_ANNOUNCE is clear), requests default negotiation and goes to PROBE_TUR_FOR_NEGOTIATION (route b) if the device changed, else releases the CCB and breaks (route c). PROBE_TUR_FOR_NEGOTIATION and PROBE_DV_EXIT either start domain validation (PROBE_INQUIRY_BASIC_DV1, route b) or finish: clear CAM_DEV_UNCONFIGURED/acquire, clear the DV flags, announce AC_FOUND_DEVICE unless PROBE_NO_ANNOUNCE, set PROBE_DONE, release the CCB and break (route c); PROBE_INQUIRY_BASIC_DV1/DV2 compare the inquiry data and on mismatch back off (to PROBE_TUR_FOR_NEGOTIATION) or go to PROBE_DV_EXIT (route b), on match move DV1 to DV2 (route b) or finish like the TUR case (route c). Any other action panics. The CCB is therefore not released on the outr route and is released on the others.

Orig reviewer RIGHT (outr returns without releasing the CCB, 1179-1182). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the realloc branch leaves the action PROBE_REPORT_LUNS (1324-1335, no PROBE_SET_ACTION there). name: scsi_scan_bus
prose: Slice cut the head: static void scsi_scan_bus(struct cam_periph *periph, union ccb *request_ccb) is at scsi_xpt.c:1933-2285. Precondition: request_ccb has func_code XPT_SCAN_BUS, XPT_SCAN_TGT or XPT_SCAN_LUN; for XPT_SCAN_BUS and XPT_SCAN_TGT the caller holds the path mutex xpt_path_mtx(path) (it is unlocked at 2032 and relocked at 2069); for XPT_SCAN_LUN the CCB was issued by this function with CAM_UNLOCKED and ccb_h.ppriv_ptr0 pointing at the scsi_scan_bus_info, and no path mutex is held on entry (it is taken at 2095). Postcondition (returns nothing). XPT_SCAN_BUS and XPT_SCAN_TGT: it allocates a work CCB with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait; on NULL it completes request_ccb with CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL via xpt_done and returns (1951-1956); a failed path inquiry completes request_ccb with the inquiry status after freeing the work CCB (1957-1963); if the HBA has PIM_NOINITIATOR it completes with CAM_REQ_CMP after freeing the work CCB (1965-1973); on certain HBAs it sends an XPT_RESET_BUS and a failure completes request_ccb with that status, freeing both CCBs (1977-1992); it allocates a scan_info (M_NOWAIT) and on NULL completes with CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL after freeing the work CCB (1997-2003). Otherwise it records request_ccb and the path inquiry data in scan_info, picks the target range (the single target for XPT_SCAN_TGT, target 0 only for PIM_SEQSCAN, else all targets), unlocks the path mutex, and for each target other than the initiator creates a path and a work CCB and issues an XPT_SCAN_LUN with xpt_action; a failed xpt_create_path or CCB allocation inside the loop calls free_scan_info, completes request_ccb with that status (or CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL) and breaks, which can leave already-issued XPT_SCAN_LUN CCBs still referring to the freed scan_info (2034-2067). It relocks the path mutex and returns with it held (2069). XPT_SCAN_LUN: it locks the path mutex and the target luns_mtx and decides the next LUN: with a REPORT LUNS list it steps lunindex[target_id] (skipping LUN 0 if it was the first entry and index 0), picking the next LUN, or marks the target finished; without a list it probes the next configured device's LUN or increments lun_id up to the HBA max_lun subject to quirk and device-flag tests (2094-2180). If another LUN of the same target remains, it frees the old path, creates a path for it and reuses request_ccb as the next XPT_SCAN_LUN (a failed xpt_create_path jumps to hop_again) (2253-2277). If the target is finished it frees the old path and updates the scan counter at hop_again: for XPT_SCAN_TGT done is true at once; for PIM_SEQSCAN the counter increments (skipping the initiator id) and the scan is done when it reaches max_target + 1; otherwise the counter decrements and the scan is done when it reaches 0. When done it unlocks the mutex, frees request_ccb, takes the original request from scan_info, frees scan_info (free_scan_info) and completes the original with CAM_REQ_CMP via xpt_done (2212-2222). When not done and PIM_SEQSCAN is not set it unlocks the mutex and frees request_ccb without issuing a new CCB (the other in-flight per-target CCBs continue the scan) (2225-2229). When not done with PIM_SEQSCAN it creates a path for the next target (a failure frees request_ccb, frees scan_info and completes the original with that status, 2230-2244), else reuses request_ccb as an XPT_SCAN_LUN. In the reuse cases it unlocks the mutex and calls xpt_action(request_ccb) (2278-2279). The path mutex is not held on return from the XPT_SCAN_LUN case and is held on return from the XPT_SCAN_BUS/XPT_SCAN_TGT case. Any other func_code does nothing (2282-2283).
note: scsi_xpt.c:1933-2285 read in full except comments and debug prints. Orig-round reviewer RIGHT (non-PIM_SEQSCAN path frees request_ccb at 2225-2228 without issuing another CCB or completing the original, unless the scan is done); the path mutex 'left unlocked' claim in the old prose was wrong for XPT_SCAN_BUS/TGT (relocked at 2069). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT (PIM_SEQSCAN reuses the CCB, 2245-2251). Possible use of freed scan_info after loop failure (2046-2049) noted, not proven reachable.

name: dtrace_ecb_resize
prose: Precondition: ecb and ecb->dte_state are valid; ecb->dte_action is a list of actions meeting the ASSERTs (debug-only): every record has dtrd_size > 0 or dtrd_alignment == 1 (11244); each aggregation has nonzero dtrd_size, non-NULL dtag_first, a predecessor with dta_intuple set and aggbase/curneeded already established (11252-11256); a non-tuple, non-aggregation action must not follow directly a tuple action (11293-11294). Several tuple (dta_intuple) records in a row are allowed: only the first of a group needs a non-tuple predecessor (11276-11277). Postcondition (dtrace.c:11229-11321): sets ecb->dte_size = sizeof(dtrace_rechdr_t) and ecb->dte_alignment = sizeof(dtrace_epid_t), then walks the action list: dte_alignment becomes the MAX with each record's alignment; an aggregation gets dtag_base = aggbase, its record offset is curneeded rounded up to its alignment, curneeded advances by dtrd_size, dte_needed = MAX(dte_needed, curneeded), and aggbase/curneeded are reset to UINT32_MAX (11249-11268); a tuple record starts curneeded (and aggbase) from dte_size with the aggid phase if curneeded was UINT32_MAX, gets its offset from curneeded rounded up and advances curneeded without changing dte_size (11269-11290); any other record gets an offset at dte_size rounded up to its alignment, advances dte_size by dtrd_size and raises dte_needed to at least dte_size (11291-11302). At each of the three size additions, if the sum wraps below the earlier value it returns EINVAL immediately (11262-11263, 11288-11289, 11299-11300), keeping all assignments already made. After the loop, if the action list is non-empty, is not a lone DTRACEACT_SPECULATE and dte_size still equals sizeof(dtrace_rechdr_t), dte_size is set to 0 (11306-11314). It then rounds dte_size and dte_needed up to sizeof(dtrace_epid_t) (dte_needed is not reset at entry, only MAX-updated), sets ecb->dte_state->dts_needed = MAX(dts_needed, dte_needed) and returns 0 (11316-11320). No locks are taken here.
note: dtrace.c:11229-11321 read in full. Round-1 reviewer RIGHT (dte_needed and dts_needed only MAX-updated), round-2 RIGHT (overflow returns EINVAL at 11262, 11288, 11299), round-15 RIGHT (consecutive tuple records allowed: assertion 11276-11277 only applies when curneeded == UINT32_MAX).

name: dtrace_ecb_action_add
prose: Slice cut the head: static int dtrace_ecb_action_add(dtrace_ecb_t *ecb, dtrace_actdesc_t *desc) is at dtrace.c:11535-11782. Precondition: the caller holds dtrace_lock; ecb, ecb->dte_state and its dts_options are valid; for DTRACEACT_PRINTM desc->dtad_difo must be non-NULL because it is dereferenced without a NULL test (11710). Postcondition: for an aggregating kind it returns EINVAL if the existing chain already has a DTRACEACT_COMMIT or DTRACEACT_SPECULATE, or if dtrace_ecb_aggregation_create returns NULL (11549-11567). For other kinds it first sets state->dts_destructive for destructive kinds (or a DIFEXPR whose DIF is destructive) (11569-11573), then switches on the kind: PRINTF/PRINTA/SYSTEM/FREOPEN/DIFEXPR take a format via dtrace_format_add when arg != 0 (11576-11597; this adds a format to the state even if a later check returns EINVAL); LIBACT, TRACEMEM, TRACEMEM_DYNSIZE return EINVAL for a NULL DIF and for a string result without DIF_TF_BYREF (11599-11613); STACK, JSTACK, USTACK compute the record size from the frame count and string size options; SYM and MOD need a non-NULL DIF whose result size is 8 and is not BYREF, USYM/UMOD/UADDR need the same; STOP/BREAKPOINT/PANIC need nothing, CHILL/DISCARD/RAISE need a DIF; EXIT needs a DIF of result size sizeof(int) and not BYREF; SPECULATE returns EINVAL if ecb->dte_size > sizeof(dtrace_rechdr_t) or the DIF is NULL and otherwise sets state->dts_speculates (11699-11707); COMMIT returns EINVAL if a COMMIT already exists or the DIF is NULL; any other kind returns EINVAL (11726-11727). Then, when the record size is nonzero or the kind is SPECULATE, it returns EINVAL if the chain already contains a DTRACEACT_COMMIT (11730-11742); otherwise it kmem_zallocs a dtrace_action_t (KM_SLEEP) with dtrd_size = size. For both branches it sets dta_refcnt = 1, computes the record alignment from the size (a power of two, up to 8), fills dta_kind, dta_difo (taking a dtrace_difo_hold reference when non-NULL), dtrd_action, arg, uarg, alignment and format, appends the action to the end of the ecb's chain (updating dte_action and dte_action_last) and returns 0 (11748-11781). EINVAL returns can follow earlier side effects: dts_destructive, dts_speculates and dtrace_format_add are not undone. No other locks are taken.
note: dtrace.c:11535-11782 read (comments and ASSERT lines skipped). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: unsupported kind (default at 11726) and SPECULATE with dte_size > header (11700-11701) return EINVAL; the old prose listed them as preconditions. Slice cut head; name outside slice was the only other reviewer reason.

name: dtrace_state_go
prose: Slice cut the head: static int dtrace_state_go(dtrace_state_t *state, processorid_t *cpu) is at dtrace.c:15002-15314. Precondition: the caller holds neither cpu_lock nor dtrace_lock (both are taken at 15014-15015), state is valid and *cpu is writable. Postcondition: rval starts at 0; every return passes through out, which releases dtrace_lock and cpu_lock and returns rval (15309-15313). EBUSY if dts_activity is not INACTIVE (15017-15019); it then calls dtrace_enabling_prime; EACCES if the state is destructive and its credential is not (15028-15031); dtrace_state_prereserve; ENOMEM if DTRACEOPT_NSPEC exceeds INT_MAX or the speculation array (kmem_zalloc, KM_NOSLEEP) fails (15043-15054); it stores the speculation array and count in the state, and allocates one per-CPU buffer array per speculation, jumping to err (ENOMEM) on failure (15059-15067). If DTRACEOPT_GRABANON is set it returns ENOENT when dtrace_anon.dta_state is NULL, EALREADY if state->dts_necbs != 0 (both via out, without freeing the speculation arrays just allocated), otherwise grabs the anonymous state, makes it the 'state' used from then on, copies the option, stores *cpu = dtrace_anon.dta_beganon (15092) and, if that anonymous state is not INACTIVE, goes to out with rval 0 without allocating more buffers for it (the grabbing state keeps its speculation arrays) (15069-15101). It then adjusts the AGGSIZE, BUFSIZE and SPECSIZE options, returns ENOSPC (via out) if a required size is below sizeof(uint64_t) (15143-15155), calls dtrace_state_buffers (a nonzero result goes to err), tries dtrace_dstate_init for the dynamic variable state with halving sizes unless BUFRESIZE is manual (a final failure goes to err with the last error), clamps the status and clean rates, registers the cleaner and deadman (callouts on FreeBSD), sets dts_activity = WARMUP (15216), disables interrupts, stores *cpu = curcpu (15243), clears the DTRACEBUF_INACTIVE flag of that CPU's buffer, fires the BEGIN probe, re-enables interrupts, changes WARMUP to ACTIVE if still WARMUP (15257-15258), activates the buffers (per CPU for the anonymous state, else by dtrace_xcall) and goes to out with rval 0. The err path frees dts_buffer and dts_aggbuffer and the speculation buffers and array and resets dts_nspeculations and dts_speculations (15285-15307) before falling into out with the error. Failures through out other than err do not free the speculation array. *cpu is therefore written on the grabanon path (15092) and on the normal start path, and may already be modified when a later step fails on the grabanon path.
note: dtrace.c:15002-15314 read in full (ASSERT and comment lines skipped). Orig reviewer RIGHT (grabanon early return with rval 0, 15100-15101). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the speculation array and per-CPU speculation buffers are allocated (15048-15067) before the grabanon branch, so the grabanon early return has already allocated them for the grabbing state, though no main buffers/dynvars are allocated for it.

name: dtrace_speculation_commit
prose: Precondition: state is valid, cpu is a processor id with entries in the speculation and primary buffer arrays, which is a speculation id; it takes no lock and runs in probe context (dtrace.c:2867-3027). Postcondition (returns nothing): which == 0 returns at once (2877-2878); which > state->dts_nspeculations sets CPU_DTRACE_ILLOP in cpu_core[cpu].cpuc_dtrace_flags and returns (2880-2883). Otherwise it loops on a compare-and-swap of spec->dtsp_state: if the current state is DTRACESPEC_COMMITTINGMANY it leaves the loop without any state change (2892-2893); INACTIVE and DISCARDING return (2896-2898); COMMITTING returns (2900-2909); ACTIVE becomes COMMITTING; ACTIVEONE becomes COMMITTING when this CPU's speculative buffer has dtb_offset != 0, else (falls through) COMMITTINGMANY; ACTIVEMANY becomes COMMITTINGMANY (2911-2937). It then calls dtrace_buffer_reserve(dest, src->dtb_offset, ...); on a negative result it calls dtrace_buffer_drop(dest) and goes to out without copying (2944-2948). On success it stamps every record in the speculative buffer with the current dtrace_gethrtime (2957-2978), copies src->dtb_offset bytes to the reserved place in dest and sets dest->dtb_offset = offs + src->dtb_offset (2986-3009). At out, on both the failure and success routes, if the original state was ACTIVE, or ACTIVEONE which was moved to COMMITTING, it CASes COMMITTING back to INACTIVE (3016-3022); a speculation that moved to or already was COMMITTINGMANY is left in that state for a later cleaner. In every route that reaches out it sets src->dtb_offset = 0, adds src->dtb_drops to src->dtb_xamot_drops and zeroes src->dtb_drops (3024-3026).
note: dtrace.c:2867-3027 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (reserve failure path appends nothing, 2944-2948). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: COMMITTINGMANY breaks out of the CAS loop without a state change (2892-2893) and the COMMITTING->INACTIVE CAS happens on both success and failure (3016-3022).

name: DTRACE_LOADFUNC(bits)
prose: Generated functions uint8_t dtrace_load8(uintptr_t addr), uint16_t dtrace_load16, uint32_t dtrace_load32 and uint64_t dtrace_load64, produced by the macro DTRACE_LOADFUNC(bits) at dtrace.c:523-560 and instantiated at 740-743. Precondition: called from probe context, so that cpu_core[curcpu].cpuc_dtrace_flags is the current CPU's flag word; addr is the address to read. Postcondition: with size = bits / 8 it first expands DTRACE_ALIGNCHECK, which on architectures other than x86 and aarch64 (the guard at 477) sets CPU_DTRACE_BADALIGN in the flags, stores addr in cpuc_dtrace_illval and returns 0 when addr is not aligned to size, and which expands to nothing on x86 and aarch64 (485). It then scans dtrace_toxrange[0 .. dtrace_toxranges-1]: if the interval [addr, addr + size) overlaps an entry (addr below dtt_limit and addr + size above dtt_base) it sets CPU_DTRACE_BADADDR, stores addr in cpuc_dtrace_illval and returns 0 (537-549). Otherwise it sets CPU_DTRACE_NOFAULT in the flags, reads the value with a volatile load, clears CPU_DTRACE_NOFAULT and returns the loaded value if CPU_DTRACE_FAULT is not set, else 0 (552-559). A fault during the load is caught by the trap handler (which sets CPU_DTRACE_FAULT) and is not handled in this code.
note: dtrace.c:477-486, 523-560, 740-743. Previously dropped (name not a C name); now fixed under the macro name. Added the architecture guard on the alignment check, which the old prose stated unconditionally; reviewers had only the 'name' complaint. The trap-handler role is outside this file section and not verified.

name: dtrace_dif_emulate
prose: Slice is a middle fragment: the function is uint64_t dtrace_dif_emulate(dtrace_difo_t *difo, dtrace_mstate_t *mstate, dtrace_vstate_t *vstate, dtrace_state_t *state) at dtrace.c:6125-6931. Precondition: difo is a DIF object that passed the DIF validator, mstate, vstate and state are valid for the current CPU; it runs in probe context. Postcondition: it sets mstate->dtms_difo = difo (6155) and the fixed register %r0 to 0 (6157), then loops while pc < difo->dtdo_len and CPU_DTRACE_FAULT is not set in cpu_core[curcpu].cpuc_dtrace_flags (6159), fetching one instruction per iteration (opc is the offset of the instruction being executed) and switching on its opcode. Arithmetic and logic opcodes write regs[rd]; for the division and remainder opcodes a zero divisor sets CPU_DTRACE_DIVZERO in the flags and regs[rd] = 0 (6192-6224), without changing cpuc_dtrace_illval; bad addresses and misalignment on loads and stores are reported through other CPU flag bits and the illval slot, as the load and store cases (for example 6880-6918) show, and an unaligned or non-storable store breaks out of the instruction without storing. DIF_OP_RET (6381) records the returned value in rval and ends the program (rval = regs[rd]; pc = textlen, 6382-6383). When the loop ends, if CPU_DTRACE_FAULT is not set it returns rval (0 if no RET ran), otherwise it stores opc * sizeof(dif_instr_t) in mstate->dtms_fltoffs, sets DTRACE_MSTATE_FLTOFFS in mstate->dtms_present and returns 0 (6924-6930). It takes no locks and takes no references; depending on the executed instructions it can write scratch space, statics, thread-local and dynamic variables through the helper functions, and memory that dtrace_canstore allows.
note: dtrace.c:6125-6931, slice cut head and tail. PARTLY READ: I read the declarations, loop head, the arithmetic and division cases (6168-6224) and the tail (6880-6931) and grepped the rest; the ~600 lines of load/store, variable, call, branch and tuple opcode cases (about 6225-6880) were not read line by line. Round-17 reviewer RIGHT: division by zero sets CPU_DTRACE_DIVZERO and regs[rd] = 0 (6193-6195).

name: dtrace_probe
prose: Slice is the middle of void dtrace_probe(dtrace_id_t id, uintptr_t arg0, ..., uintptr_t arg4) at dtrace.c:7346-8040; the packet name is not a name in the file. Precondition: called by a provider when probe id fires, in a context where it may run with interrupts as the provider arranged. Postcondition (returns nothing): it returns at once (before any other work) if the kernel has panicked (7361 and 7392); otherwise it calls dtrace_probe_enter(id), looks up the probe, and when not on an interrupt and the probe's predicate cache matches the current thread's cached id it exits (7379-7387). It then fills mstate with the timestamp, probe and arguments and loops over the probe's ECB list (7419). For each ECB: if state->dts_activity is not ACTIVE it skips the ECB (with a special case that moves the state to DRAINING for the BEGIN probe when it is not WARMUP, 7459-7480); the user-mode and owner conditions in dte_cond can skip it; if now - state->dts_alive exceeds dtrace_deadman_timeout and the state lacks kernel-destructive permission (or destructive actions are disallowed) it CAS-sets the state's activity to DTRACE_ACTIVITY_KILLED and skips the ECB (7544-7566; I did not read the comment-only continuation lines to confirm that path ends with continue); it reserves dte_needed bytes in the CPU buffer with dtrace_buffer_reserve and skips the ECB if that fails (7568); it writes the record header (epid and timestamp) when dte_size != 0 (7575-7586); a predicate, if present, is run by dtrace_dif_emulate and a false result may update probe->dtpr_predcache / curthread->t_predcache and skips the ECB (7596-7615). It then runs the actions in list order until CPU_DTRACE_ERROR is set (7617): aggregations call dtrace_aggregate with the computed value; the privilege-gated actions (STOP, BREAKPOINT, PANIC, STACK, JSTACK/USTACK, SYM/MOD, USYM/UMOD/UADDR, CHILL, RAISE) only act when the matching dtrace_priv_* check allows it; SPECULATE redirects the record into a speculation buffer; COMMIT and DISCARD call the speculation commit/discard; EXIT CAS-moves the state to DRAINING; DIF-expression-like actions store the DIF result by value or by reference into the record. After the actions, a CPU_DTRACE_FAULT increments buf->dtb_errors and reports an error probe (continuing to the next ECB, 7985-8029); otherwise, if the record was not already committed it sets buf->dtb_offset = offs + ecb->dte_size (8032-8033). After the loop it restores the thread's virtual-time start, and calls dtrace_probe_exit(cookie) (8036-8039). So not every ECB runs its actions and the record header is conditional on the ECB size.
note: dtrace.c:7346-8040, PARTLY READ: lines 7346-7860 and 7860-8040 read with comment lines and ASSERT/DTRACE_STORE lines filtered out; the small per-action details (e.g. the exact skip statements after 7469, 7495, 7525, 7565 and some PRINTM size checks) were not verified individually and the end of the deadman branch was not confirmed to be a continue. Round-17 reviewer RIGHT: header is written only when dte_size != 0 (7575) and privilege-gated actions are skipped (e.g. 7654-7665).

name: ctf_decl_push
prose: Precondition: cd was set up by ctf_decl_init, lc describes a loaded CTF section, type is a CTF type id; recursion depth follows the type graph and is not bounded in this function. Postcondition (fbt.c:947-1028; returns nothing): if ctf_lookup_by_id(lc, type) is NULL it sets cd->cd_err = ENOENT and returns without appending (958-961). Otherwise it reads the kind and the referenced type index t and switches on the kind: CTF_K_ARRAY pushes the array's content type recursively, sets n to the element count and prec = CTF_PREC_ARRAY; CTF_K_TYPEDEF with an empty name (ctf_type_rname(lc, tp)[0] == 0) pushes the referenced type t and returns without appending a node for this type, while a typedef with a non-empty name does not push the referenced type and gets prec = CTF_PREC_BASE (974-980); CTF_K_FUNCTION and CTF_K_POINTER push t first and use CTF_PREC_FUNCTION or CTF_PREC_POINTER; CTF_K_VOLATILE, CTF_K_CONST and CTF_K_RESTRICT push t first and take prec = cd->cd_qualp (marked as qualifiers); every other kind uses CTF_PREC_BASE and pushes nothing (966-1002). For all those kinds other than the empty-name typedef it then mallocs a node (M_WAITOK) with the type, kind and n, sets cd->cd_order[prec] = cd->cd_ordp++ if cd->cd_nodes[prec] was empty, raises cd->cd_qualp to prec when prec > cd_qualp and prec < CTF_PREC_ARRAY, and prepends the node for arrays and for qualifiers whose prec is CTF_PREC_BASE, else appends it to cd->cd_nodes[prec] (1004-1027). A failed lookup inside a nested push only sets cd_err = ENOENT; this node is still appended by the outer call.

name: sign_extend64
prose: Precondition: index is an int that should be in 0..63; for any other value the shift amount shift = 63 - index (a uint8_t) is outside 0..63 and the shifts are undefined or wrong. Postcondition: it computes shift = (uint8_t)(63 - index), shifts value left by shift in uint64_t arithmetic (discarding bits above index), converts the result to int64_t and arithmetic-shifts it right by shift (sign-propagating, relying on the implementation's behaviour for right-shifting a negative signed value), and returns that as uint64_t (bitops.h:425-430). For index in 0..62 the result is value's low index + 1 bits sign-extended from bit index (the upper bits of the result are copies of bit index of value); for index 63, shift is 0 and value is returned unchanged. For example index 0 gives 0 or all ones. It reads only its arguments and has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= index && index <= 63; ensures index == 63 ==> result == value; */
note: bitops.h:424-430. Earlier contracts were falsified by random testing (value=207 index=0 gives all ones), so the contract was reduced to the one property that holds by inspection (index 63 returns value). Prose fixed to state that bits above the field are discarded before extension and the dependence on arithmetic right shift.

name: _h2b

name: ieee80211_hdrlen
prose: Precondition: fc is a little-endian 802.11 frame-control field (type __le16, taken by value; the function has no side effects and takes no locks). Postcondition (ieee80211.h:912-949): if ieee80211_is_ctl(fc) (FC0 type bits equal to control) it switches on the subtype bits of the FC0 octet: CTS (0xc0) or ACK (0xd0) returns sizeof(struct ieee80211_frame_ack) (frame control 2, duration 2, RA 6 = 10 bytes), BAR (0x80) returns sizeof(struct ieee80211_frame_bar) (fc 2, dur 2, RA 6, TA 6, BAR control 2, sequence 2 = 20 bytes, net80211/ieee80211.h:707-715) and any other control subtype returns sizeof(struct ieee80211_frame_min) (fc 2, dur 2, addr1 6, addr2 6 = 16 bytes). For a non-control frame it starts from sizeof(struct ieee80211_frame) (24 bytes); if the frame is a data frame it adds IEEE80211_ADDR_LEN (6) when the direction bits are DSTODS (0x03), and adds sizeof(uint16_t) (2) when FC0 has the QoS-data subtype bit with data type (the (fc & (0x80|0x0c)) == (0x80|0x08) test); the management-frame test at 940 only has a no-op body. It returns that size as an unsigned int.

name: linuxkpi_ieee80211_ifattach
prose: Slice cut the head: int linuxkpi_ieee80211_ifattach(struct ieee80211_hw *hw) is at linux_80211.c:7383-7687 (the packet's unnamed function). Precondition: hw is an initialised struct ieee80211_hw with its wiphy and lkpi_hw (HW_TO_LHW(hw)) and net80211 com ic set up, ic not yet attached. Postcondition: it allocates lhw->workq with alloc_ordered_workqueue(wiphy_name(hw->wiphy), 0) and returns -EAGAIN at once if that is NULL (7393-7395). Otherwise it sets ic->ic_macaddr from wiphy->perm_addr if non-zero, else from the first wiphy address, else prints a warning and leaves it (7398-7407); sets phytype, opmode STA and the base capability bits (WPA, monitor, optional WME, short slot and preamble, optional BGSCAN when ops->hw_scan exists), calls lkpi_enable_hw_scan (its result is not used), sets frag and A-MPDU offload flags from hw flags, and, when the wiphy reports available antennas and lkpi_80211_mo_get_antenna returns 0, sets ic_rxstream and ic_txstream from the antenna masks (7414-7472). With LKPI_80211_HW_CRYPTO and lkpi_hwcrypto set and cipher suites present it computes hardware ciphers (TKIP only when lkpi_hwcrypto_tkip, otherwise AES-CCM/GCM-128 only) and calls ieee80211_set_hardware_ciphers (7474-7517). It then calls lkpi_ic_getradiocaps for the channels, ieee80211_ifattach(ic), installs the lkpi_ic_* method pointers, saves the original scan, node and (with LKPI_80211_HT and ampdu_action) A-MPDU method pointers in lhw and replaces them (7519-7583), calls lkpi_radiotap_attach, and loops over the wiphy bands: it counts bands with channels in lhw->supbands, raises lhw->max_rates to the largest n_bitrates and, while hw->conf.chandef.chan is still NULL, sets conf.chandef and lhw->dflt_chandef from the first non-disabled channel found (7593-7629). max_rates is clamped to IEEE80211_RATE_MAXSIZE with a message (7634-7638). It computes lhw->scan_ie_len from the rate sizes and optional DS-param, HT and VHT elements (7647-7667); if hw->wiphy->max_scan_ie_len is nonzero and scan_ie_len exceeds it, it jumps to err and returns -EAGAIN (7670-7672, 7684-7686) after the attachment steps above have already been done (the err label only has a TODO comment and returns, so the workqueue from 7393 and the net80211 attachment are not undone, 7684-7686), else it reduces max_scan_ie_len by scan_ie_len. It announces the device when bootverbose and returns 0 (7676-7683). Ownership of hw, lhw and ic remains with the caller.
